newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS HER FIRST WORLD CUP SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS HER FIRST WORLD CUP SLALOM.

text.p: Italian Deborah Compagnoni reaped the rewards of five years of intense slalom training on Sunday when she scored the first World Cup victory of her career in the technical discipline.
The reigning Olympic and world giant slalom champion, 26, kept her composure and performed two near-perfect runs on an icy Hrischenkogel piste in bitter temperatures of minus 17 degrees celsius.

She was fastest in both and clocked a total time of one minute 42.94 seconds to win by more than a full second for the eighth victory of her career -- which also includes the super-g gold at the 1992 Olympics.
An overjoyed Compagnoni said: "I trained a lot of slalom over the past five years but never managed to win a race. Semmering really brings me luck."

"I have a good team around me. We did a lot of good training over the summer. This could be the reason for my success this weekend," added the Italian, who decided to miss all super-g races this season.

"I am also really pleased because this past summer was my first summer without a serious injury or illness," said Compagnoni, who missed the first half of last season when she was forced to undergo her third knee operation.
Compagnoni was second in the first of two successive slaloms at this small resort some 70 kms southwest of Vienna on Saturday, her fourth runner-up finish in slalom during her career.
France's Patricia Chauvet profited from Austrian Elfi Eder's failure to complete the second run to improve one place to second in 1:43.99.

Austrian-born Claudia Riegler, who has chosen to represent her mother's country of New Zealand after a dispute with the Austrian ski federation, improved three places in the second run to take third in 1:44.65.
Like famous compatriot Alberto Tomba, Compagnoni has trained apart from the Italian team for the past two years with coach Dino Pietrogiovanna.
Her coach was formerly a skier of the Italian "Avalanche" team which was virtually invincible from 1970 to 1976 and included ski legends Gustavo Thoeni and Piero Gros.
Riegler, a jovial 20-year-old, finished a mere hundredth of a second ahead of rival Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden, who was outside the top 10 in the first leg before advancing to fourth.

"My performance this weekend was not the greatest," said Riegler, who was ninth on Saturday. "But I learned a lot from my mistakes. The problem about winning is that you are so happy you forget to check your mistakes."
Riegler is second in the slalom standings, 21 points behind Wiberg and 69 ahead of Compagnoni.
Wiberg, Saturday's winner, had been second to Riegler in both previous slaloms of the winter in Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana.
The 26-year-old Swede increased her lead in the overall World Cup standings which she snatched from Germany's Katja Seizinger on Saturday.
World Cup title holder Seizinger opted to skip the Semmering races to train for super-g and downhill.
The women's circuit moves on to Maribor, Slovenia, for a giant slalom and slalom on Jan 3 and 4.
